title: post-shift-refactor-tactics-graham
content:
Context: quick brain dump after reviewing PR #4821 (ctx-kv cache refactor). Late-night notes — rough order: immediate risks, small safety mitigations, quick tests to ask for, follow-ups, and a tiny rollout plan. Save as a scratchpad; will formalize later if we decide to ship.
High-level summary of PR seen:
- Removes a layer of indirection in KV cache lookup to reduce per-token branching and memory churn.
- Introduces a new lightweight cacheEntry struct and changes serialization format for warm-start snapshots.
- Adds two new flags: --kv-conservative-scan and --kv-snapshot-version=2.

Immediate red flags / unknowns (what worried me while reading):
1) Backwards compatibility: snapshot format change is not gated behind a migration path. If a node loads an old snapshot with the new code path, what happens? (unclear from code)
2) Concurrency: small window where cacheEntry is updated concurrently while kv-evict worker iterates — I saw a Mutex swapped for an RW lock but not full reasoning.
3) Memory accounting: new struct adds a small header; we need to ensure telemetry tags (mem-per-frame) still line up.
4) Hot path performance claim: benchmark in PR shows -8% p95 CPU, but the fixture used 1k sequence length. Need real distribution run (seqs 8/64/256 mix).

Quick immediate asks to require before merging (fast, unblock-friendly):
- Add a quick fallback toggle (env var or flag) to bypass new path at runtime: --kv-fallback-enable. Must be easy to flip via SSM/console.
- Add a tiny compatibility unit test: load a v1 snapshot then assert Load() doesn't crash and read path falls back to v1 behavior when flag off.
- Add a short comment explaining why the RW lock is sufficient (link to ticket/benchmark) or prefer to reintroduce per-shard Mutex if reason unclear.
- Add a note to PR description about schema change and what customers (Dedicated/Private) will observe.

Small reproducible checks I ran locally (commands to ask author to include as CI or reviewer-run checklist):
- repro 1: run small integration with old snapshot
  git checkout origin/main && \
  make -C infra/caches build && \
  ./bin/kv-sim --load-snapshot testdata/snap-v1.bin --run-workload quick
  expect: no crash, outputs same eviction counts within 5%.
- repro 2: microbench (seq distribution):
  ./bench/kv_micro --seq-dist="8:0.6,64:0.3,256:0.1" --iters=2000
  compare cpu and allocation traces vs main branch.

Reviewer checklist (quick):
- [ ] CI coverage: unit tests + integration snapshot load
- [ ] Telemetry: mem counters, per-request allocs, p95 CPU in bench smoke
- [ ] Rollback toggle exists and documented
- [ ] Migration note in CHANGELOG + ops playbook updated
- [ ] Code comments where concurrency assumptions are made

Risk matrix (quick notes):
- Low: cosmetic renames, simple helpers
- Med: new struct memory overhead might spike in high-concurrency workloads (Dedicated pools)
- High: snapshot format mismatch causing load failures on restart (customer impact)

Minimal safe rollout plan (if we go forward):
1) Merge behind feature flag default-off (server flag --kv-snapshot-version=2 disabled in production config).
2) Canary: enable for internal test cluster only (0 traffic external) for 24h — run synthetic workloads (seq mix above) + end-to-end chat flows.
3) Prod small canary: enable on 2/40 nodes receiving <1% traffic. Monitor tail latency and error budget.
4) Full rollout only after 48h stable with automated rollback threshold: +10% p99 latency or +5% error rate.
5) If any snapshot load error observed, flip flag off and open an incident (follow rollback steps below).

Rollback steps (keep this inside PR and ops playbook):
- Immediate: set --kv-fallback-enable=true on affected nodes via SSM param update or console.
- If that fails: deploy previous build (main before PR) to the group (can use blue/green deploy via infra playbook).
- Postmortem: capture snapshot files, logs, core dumps, and measure how many affected snapshots existed.

Follow-ups (non-blocking, but should land within 2 weeks):
- Add snapshot compatibility shim: read v1 format and convert to v2 lazily on load (avoid full rewrite).
- Add fuzz tests for concurrent loads/evicts (stress harness: 1000 threads, random ops).
- Perf: run a 24h run on Dedicated-like instance types and collect allocation profiles.
- Docs: ops note explaining how to toggle flags in Dedicated and Private deployments (who to contact).

Decision notes (my quick take):
- The idea is promising — fewer branches on hot path is good. But schema/snapshot change is the main blocker; needs compatibility or opt-in flagging.
- Prefer gating the rollout behind a runtime flag and a conservative canary window.

To do (me / short next steps):
- Post this as a comment in the PR summarizing asks (deadline: tomorrow morning).
- Draft a minimal CHANGELOG blurb for ops and a one-paragraph note for customer-facing release notes.
- If author says tests are expensive, offer to help write the tiny snapshot-load test.

Notes-to-self (loose ideas for longer-term):
- Consider adding a "snapshot-version-negotiation" API: node announces version at connect, client can convert or refuse.
- Think about embedding a small schema-version header into snapshots to make future changes safer.

Unanswered questions / things to ask author in PR comment:
- Why was RW lock chosen vs per-shard Mutex? (benchmarks?)
- Are there backward compatibility guarantees we must uphold for Dedicated/Private?
- Has anyone attempted the seq-distribution perf test on a machine similar to prod nodes?

End of dump. Keep short and actionable in PR comment. Will tidy into RFC if we decide to adopt.
